titulo: Spatial dynamics of infrastructure development across Indian states
palavras_chave: infrastructure development; Sustainable Development Goals; fiscal capacity; government spending; spatial autocorrelation; intergovernmental transfers; regional disparities; Indian states; development traps; governance quality; absorptive capacity
resumo: Progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals across India’s states has been spatially uneven, and most subnational assessments treat infrastructure indicators in isolation, leaving open how sectoral performance and fiscal capacity jointly shape regional outcomes. This study develops the Holistic Infrastructure Development Index (HIDI), a composite scalar that combines four infrastructure-relevant SDG dimensions-water and sanitation (SDG 6), clean energy (SDG 7), industry and infrastructure (SDG 9), and sustainable cities (SDG 11) with state-level per-capita public expenditure, used here as a proxy for the spending dimension of fiscal capacity and treated as a structural feature of each state rather than an annual flow. We use state-level SDG and fiscal data for 28 Indian states between 2018 and 2024 (N = 112), drawn from the NITI Aayog SDG India Index. We examine infrastructure convergence through complementary sigma and beta analyses, and assess the spatial structure of HIDI through Global Moran’s I with permutation inference and a Moran scatterplot reading. The data document both forms of convergence: cross-sectional dispersion falls by 12.0% over the period, and the regression of log growth on initial HIDI returns β = − 0.681, r = − 0.902, R 2 = 0.81 ( p < 0.001). Spatial autocorrelation is positive and statistically significant in every wave (Moran’s I = + 0.196 to + 0.420; pseudo- p ≤ 0.048), with stronger performers concentrated in the western–southern corridor and persistent underperformance in several northeastern states. Higher fiscal capacity does not translate uniformly into stronger infrastructure outcomes: dispersion is largest within the top fiscal quartile, a pattern we develop as the Infrastructure Fiscal Nexus Paradox, in which governance quality and absorptive capacity are associated with the resource outcome link. We organise these patterns into four illustrative development archetypes Fiscal-Augmented Performers, Efficiency-Led Performers, Catch-Up Leaders, and Development Traps and the findings indicate that intergovernmental transfers could usefully be linked not only to fiscal need but also to demonstrated implementation capacity and infrastructure outcomes.

titulo: Analisis Flypaper Effect: Pengaruh PAD dan DAU Terhadap Belanja Daerah Sumatera Selatan
autores: Anisa Cahya Ramadhani; Periansya Periansya; Choiruddin Choiruddin
palavras_chave: flypaper effect; regional own-source revenue; general allocation fund; local government spending; regional fiscal autonomy; South Sumatra; fiscal decentralization; local government finance
resumo: ABSTRACT Examining the impact of Regional Original Revenue (PAD) and General Allocation Funds (DAU) on regional expenditure posture, as well as analyzing the existence of the Flypaper Effect phenomenon within regency and city governments in South Sumatra Province, is the primary focus of this study. A quantitative approach was deployed, utilizing secondary data sourced from the official website of the Audit Board of the Republic of Indonesia (BPK RI). All 17 regencies and cities in South Sumatra were selected as the population, yielding a total of 85 observation units through a total sampling technique. Parameter estimation and hypothesis testing were processed using the panel data regression method via EViews 13 software. The empirical findings confirm that both PAD and DAU partially contribute significantly to the regional expenditure posture. Simultaneously, both funding sources are also proven to have a significant positive contribution. Furthermore, through a comparison of the regression coefficients, this study successfully demonstrates that the Flypaper Effect phenomenon is visibly confirmed within the financial management of regency and city governments across South Sumatra. Keywords: General Allocation Fund, Local Own-Source Revenue, Local Government Expenditures, Flypaper Effect. ABSTRAK Menguji dampak Pendapatan Asli Daerah (PAD) serta Dana Alokasi Umum (DAU) dalam memengaruhi postur Belanja Daerah, serta menganalisis keberadaan fenomena Flypaper Effect pada lingkup Pemerintah Kabupaten/Kota di Provinsi Sumatera Selatan adalah topik utama yang dibahas dalam kajian ini. Pendekatan kuantitatif digunakan dalam studi ini dan memanfaatkan data sekunder yang bersumber dari laman yang terstandardisasi BPK RI (www.bpk.go.id). Seluruh kabupaten/kota di Sumatera Selatan yang berjumlah 17 wilayah dijadikan sebagai populasi, dengan total 85 unit observasi melalui teknik sampling jenuh. Estimasi parameter dan pengujian hipotesis diolah menggunakan metode regresi data panel dari aplikasi EViews 13. Temuan empiris mengonfirmasi bahwa baik PAD maupun DAU secara parsial memberikan kontribusi secara signifikan terhadap postur Belanja Daerah. Melalui simultan, kedua sumber pendanaan juga terbukti berkontribusi positif signifikan. Lebih lanjut, melalui komparasi nilai koefisien regresi, kajian ini berhasil membuktikan gejala Flypaper Effect terkonfirmasi nyata pada tata kelola finansial Pemerintah Kabupaten/Kota se-Sumatera Selatan. Kata kunci: : Dana Alokasi Umum, Pendapatan Asli Daerah, Belanja Daerah, Flypaper Effect

titulo: From Devolution to Development: The Role of Fiscal Management Efficiency in Translating Fiscal Decentralization into County Economic Growth in Kenya
autores: Samwel Kipchumba Koskey; Simeon Kiptarus Nganai; Thomas Agak
periodico: Asian Journal of Economics Business and Accounting
palavras_chave: fiscal decentralization; county economic growth; intergovernmental transfers; subnational governments; local economic development; moderating effect; county budget; fiscal federalism; Kenya counties; revenue distribution
resumo: Fiscal decentralisation has become an important governance reform for promoting local economic development by transferring fiscal responsibilities, resources, and decision-making authority to subnational governments. However, the developmental benefits of decentralisation depend on the efficiency with which devolved resources are managed. This study examined the relationship between fiscal decentralisation and economic growth in Kenya’s county governments, with fiscal management efficiency as a moderating variable. Specifically, the study assessed the effects of revenue assignment, intergovernmental fiscal transfers, and expenditure autonomy on county economic growth and established whether fiscal management efficiency moderated these relationships. The study adopted a positivist research philosophy and an explanatory longitudinal panel research design. The analysis covered all 47 county governments in Kenya over the period from 2013/2014 to 2022/2023, producing 470 county-year observations. Secondary data were obtained from Gross County Product reports, county budget implementation reports, revenue-sharing reports, and audit reports from the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics (KNBS), Commission on Revenue Allocation (CRA), Controller of Budget, and Office of the Auditor-General. Economic growth was measured using annual changes in Gross County Product, while fiscal decentralisation was operationalised through revenue assignment, intergovernmental fiscal transfers, and expenditure autonomy. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, panel diagnostic tests, random-effects regression, and hierarchical regression analysis. The direct-effects model was statistically significant and explained 50.2% of the overall variation in county economic growth. Revenue assignment had a positive and statistically significant effect on economic growth (β = 0.328, p < 0.001), while expenditure autonomy also had a positive and statistically significant effect (β = 0.220, p < 0.001). However, intergovernmental fiscal transfers had a negative but statistically insignificant effect on economic growth (β = −0.021, p = 0.544). Hierarchical regression analysis showed that fiscal management efficiency significantly moderated the relationship between revenue assignment and economic growth (β = 5.165, p < 0.01, ΔR² = 0.083), intergovernmental fiscal transfers and economic growth (β = 4.215, p < 0.01, ΔR² = 0.114), and expenditure autonomy and economic growth (β = 2.413, p < 0.01, ΔR² = 0.073). The final hierarchical model explained approximately 86.1% of the variation in county economic growth. The study concludes that fiscal decentralisation contributes to county economic growth, but its effectiveness depends strongly on fiscal management efficiency. While revenue assignment and expenditure autonomy directly enhance economic performance, intergovernmental transfers alone do not guarantee growth outcomes unless accompanied by effective financial management systems. The study recommends strengthening county own-source revenue mobilisation, improving budget execution, enhancing procurement and audit compliance, and promoting performance-based fiscal governance to maximise the developmental benefits of Kenya’s devolved system.

titulo: THE IMPACT OF BRAZILIAN TAX REFORM ON SMALL MUNICIPALITIES IN THE STATE OF AMAZONAS
autores: Antonio Orismar Barbosa de Oliveira; Tássia Patricia Silva do Nascimento
palavras_chave: Brazilian tax reform; small municipalities; Amazonas; consumption tax; municipal fiscal autonomy; intergovernmental transfers; Manaus Free Trade Zone; local economic development; fiscal federalism; administrative capacity
resumo: Brazil's Tax Reform, formalized by Constitutional Amendment No. 132/2023, brought about significant changes to the consumption tax system by replacing levies such as ICMS, ISS, PIS, and COFINS with new models: the Tax on Goods and Services (IBS) and the Contribution on Goods and Services (CBS). This shift aims to simplify the tax system, reduce distortions, enhance collection efficiency, and foster greater federal balance (Alexandre Pinto, 2023). For small municipalities in the state of Amazonas, the reform is particularly significant due to regional specificities—such as reliance on intergovernmental transfers, the presence of the Manaus Free Trade Zone, and local economic heterogeneity. Many of these municipalities face technical and institutional constraints, including outdated tax collection systems and a shortage of qualified personnel—factors that may hinder their adaptation to the new tax rules (Carlos Henrique de Brito, 2021). Furthermore, the centralization of tax collection proposed under the IBS model, combined with the subsequent redistribution of revenues among federal entities, could significantly alter municipal financial autonomy and local investment capacity. As noted by Luciano Amaro (2019), tax policies that fail to account for the administrative capacity of smaller municipalities can create inter-municipal inequalities, thereby affecting regional economic development. Given this context, the present study is justified by the need to analyze the Tax Reform's impact on small municipalities in Amazonas, identifying administrative challenges, revenue collection opportunities, and effects on local economic development. Understanding these impacts is crucial for informing public administrators, scholars, and tax policymakers, ultimately contributing to more efficient and equitable fiscal planning (Antônio Carlos Gil, 2010, p. 26).

titulo: Beyond Budget Allocation: Understanding Fiscal Trade-Offs and Spending Structure in Decentralized Governments
autores: Fakriah Fakriah; Nurmila Dewi; Rusydi Rusydi
periodico: Proceedings of International Conference on Agro and Marine Industry
palavras_chave: budget allocation; capital expenditure; personnel costs; fiscal behavior; expenditure elasticity; flypaper effect; fiscal decentralization
resumo: This study aims to examine fiscal trade-offs and spending structures within the context of decentralized local governments. The primary focus is to analyze how expenditure composition and fiscal behavior influence budget allocation decisions, particularly the trade-off between operational spending and capital expenditure. This research employs a quantitative approach with descriptive and explanatory design, utilizing panel data from local government financial reports across regencies and municipalities in Aceh Province over the period 2019–2023. Panel data regression analysis is applied to investigate the relationship between spending structure, fiscal behavior, and budget allocation trade-offs. The findings reveal that local government expenditure structures are predominantly driven by operational spending, especially personnel expenditures, while capital expenditure remains relatively low and shows a declining trend. This condition reflects increasing fiscal trade-offs, where short-term expenditure priorities tend to crowd out long-term investment. Furthermore, fiscal behavior demonstrates high expenditure elasticity relative to revenue, indicating a strong dependence on central government transfers, commonly associated with the flypaper effect. Empirical results confirm that both spending structure and fiscal behavior have a significant impact on budget allocation trade-offs. This study contributes to the literature on public financial management by providing insights into the implications of fiscal decentralization on expenditure quality. Policy implications highlight the need for budget reorientation toward more productive spending and strengthening local fiscal independence to support sustainable regional development

titulo: Долговая устойчивость российских регионов: сбалансированный подход и ответственное бюджетное планирование
palavras_chave: debt sustainability; regional public debt; Russian regions; soft budget constraint; federal transfers; budgeting; reserve funds; intergovernmental transfers
resumo: The article examines theoretical and practical aspects of ensuring debt sustainability of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation. The relevance of the study is due to the need to find a balance between the use of debt financing for solving socio-economic problems and maintaining a safe level of debt burden. Existing approaches to assessing debt sustainability are analyzed, including the classical approach, Bohn’s approach, and the methodology enshrined in the Budget Code of the Russian Federation. It is shown that the current system of indicators allows fixing the actual level of sustainability but does not provide a comprehensive assessment of the effectiveness of debt policy. Special attention is paid to the problem of soft budget constraints, which manifests itself in the readiness of the federal center to provide transfers to cover deficits and service regional debt. Based on the analysis of the dynamics and structure of public debt of the Russian regions for the period 2006–2023, trends are revealed: substitution of market debt with budget loans, a decrease in the share of bond issues, and growing dependence of regions on federal support. The necessity of transitioning to a balanced approach combining compliance with regulations with a qualitative assessment of debt policy, development of market borrowing instruments, formation of reserve funds, and increased responsibility of regional authorities is substantiated. Directions for improving budget planning are proposed, including factor analysis of the debt burden, linking intergovernmental transfers with sustainability indicators, and more active use of the temporary financial administration procedure

titulo: Comparative Analysis of Local Government Administration in Nigeria and the United States: A Structured Comparative Assessment of Decentralization, Fiscal Autonomy, Administrative Capacity and Service Delivery
palavras_chave: local government; decentralization; fiscal autonomy; administrative capacity; accountability; public service delivery; Nigeria; United States; intergovernmental transfers; local government finance; state-local relations; local government accountability; comparative institutional analysis
resumo: This study comparatively examines local government administration in Nigeria and the United States through a structured documentary analysis of decentralization, fiscal autonomy, administrative capacity, accountability, and service-delivery conditions. The study responds to a common weakness in cross-national comparisons: treating each country's local governments as homogeneous institutional categories. Rather than characterizing U.S. local governments generally as possessing uniform or broad autonomy, the study recognizes that their authority is constituted principally by state law and varies across states and institutional forms, including counties, municipalities, townships, and special-purpose districts. Similarly, Nigeria is treated as a system with a common constitutional framework but substantial variation in state-local government relations andimplementation practices. The study relies exclusively on secondary evidence from constitutional and legal materials, government statistical publications, judicial decisions, official government reports, and peerreviewed scholarship. A structured comparative framework is used to assess five dimensions: legal/constitutional authority, fiscal capacity and discretion, administrative organization, accountability and participation, and service-delivery capacity. Fiscal evidence from the U.S. Census Bureau shows that U.S. local governments received about 62.6% of local general revenue from sources other than intergovernmental transfers in 2022, while intergovernmental revenue represented about 37.4%. Nigerian evidence demonstrates continued importance of Federation Account transfers, although the 2024 Supreme Court judgment on local government financial autonomy has altered the legal environment. The study therefore avoids the unsupported claim that U.S. local governments are uniformly efficient or that Nigerian councils are uniformly ineffective. Instead, it finds that institutional design, fiscal discretion, administrative professionalism, and accountability arrangements create different enabling conditions for service delivery. The paper concludes that Nigeria should learn selectively from U.S. practices—especially fiscal responsibility, professional management, transparency, performance monitoring, and locally responsive decision-making—while adapting them to Nigeria's constitutional and intergovernmental context.

titulo: Determinan Kemandirian Keuangan Daerah Pemerintah Provinsi di Indonesia
autores: Aliffia Dewi Syahda; Fajar Syaiful Akbar
periodico: Prosiding Seminar Nasional Ilmu Ekonomi dan Akuntansi
palavras_chave: regional fiscal autonomy; local own-source revenue; intergovernmental transfers; capital expenditure; provincial finance; Indonesia
resumo: This study centers on examining how locally generated revenue, intergovernmental transfers, and capital spending shape the degree of regional fiscal autonomy. A quantitative framework is applied, utilizing secondary data derived from the financial statements of provincial governments across Indonesia covering the 2021–2024 period. The interrelationships among the variables are assessed using a panel data regression approach, processed with EViews version 13. The findings reveal that regional fiscal autonomy is strongly associated with the magnitude of locally generated revenue. This suggests that the ability of subnational governments to effectively harness their own revenue sources plays a crucial role in strengthening fiscal independence. In contrast, funds transferred from the central government do not significantly contribute to enhancing such independence, as they are predominantly allocated to routine expenditures. Likewise, capital outlays have yet to demonstrate a meaningful impact, given that their benefits are long-term in nature and not immediately observable within the study period.

titulo: Fiscal Capacity, Fiscal Stress and Social Sector Spending in Indian States: Evidence from a State-Level Panel Dataset, 2005–2025
periodico: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
palavras_chave: social spending; fiscal capacity; fiscal pressure; fiscal transfers; budget deficit; public debt; Indian states
resumo: The social sector expenditure is important in promoting human development, welfare and inclusive growth especially in a federal system like India where the delivery of social services is largely the responsibility of the states. We analyse the effect of social sector expenditure on per capita GSDP, Own Tax Revenue, Fiscal Deficit, Debt and Intergovernmental Grants using 315 observations from 15 large states between 2005 and 2025. The results indicate that Intergovernmental Grants and Fiscal Deficit have significant and positive impact on Social Sector Spending at 1 percent and 5 percent level of significance and the value of correlation coefficients are 0.494 and 0.591 respectively. However, variables of economic capacity such as GSDP, Own Tax Revenue and Debt show relatively modest relationships. Multiple regression shows a R 2 of 0.626, which means that the selected variables explain 62.6 percent of the variation in spending. The F-statistic (103.378) indicates that the model is overall significant. The results point to the role of fiscal transfers and state fiscal conditions as determinants of social expenditure preferences.

titulo: The Evolution of Budgetary and Administrative Federalism in Russia: From Negotiated Decentralisation to Discretionary Centralisation (1991–2022)
palavras_chave: budget federalism; administrative federalism; intergovernmental transfers; discretionary transfers; decentralization; centralization; resource allocation; regional governors; Russian regions; 2008 financial crisis; sanctions; COVID-19 pandemic; regional integration; fiscal federalism
resumo: The article traces the evolution of the budgetary and administrative dimensions of Russian federalism in 1991–2022 and shows how consistent transformation of the institutional design of intergovernmental transfers – from negotiated decentralisation in the 1990s to formal but increasingly discretionary distribution in the 2000s–2020s – was expanding room for politically motivated resources repartition. The periodisation is built as a secondary historiographical synthesis of the works on budgetary and ad-ministrative federalism in Russia supported by the general content of key legal-normative acts; to empirically illustrate the three most recent periods an unbalanced panel of data on 84 regions of the Russian Federation for 2007–2022 was used. For each of six periods, descriptive indicators such as per capita volume of discre-tionary transfers in constant 2015 prices and the share of regional governors appointed as outsiders (“varyags”) were calculated; the analysis is descriptive rather than causal. Institutional dynamics following each of the four structural shocks – the 2008–2009 financial crisis, the 2014–2015 sanctions shock, the 2020 COVID19 pandemic, and the 2022 integration of new regions – was not accompanied by a return to formula-based allocation features: per capita discretionary transfers came up from 8.3 thousand rubles (2007–2008) to 17.6 thousand rubles (2021–22) in comparable prices, i. e. more than doubling, while the share of outsider governors rose from 34% to 57%. It is shown that accrescent administra-tive centralisation and expanding the transfer system discretionary component are two facets of a unified insti-tutional process that forms structural suppositions for the prevalence of the electoral channel of resource allo-cation over formula-based equalisation.

titulo: Trust, power, and Awareness as Determinants of Local Tax Compliance: The Moderating Role of Civic Pride in Lahat Regency, Indonesia
periodico: Ranah Research Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Development
palavras_chave: civic pride; trust in authorities; tax morale; taxpayer awareness; local own-source revenue; street lighting tax; Lahat Regency; regional fiscal independence; slippery slope framework; theory of planned behavior; moderating effect
resumo: Local Own-Source Revenue (Pendapatan Asli Daerah/PAD) is a key indicator of regional fiscal independence, yet most local governments in Indonesia remain highly dependent on intergovernmental transfers. In this context, improving local tax compliance is crucial, particularly in Lahat Regency, which relies heavily on Certain Goods and Services Tax (PBJT), Street Lighting Tax (PPJ), and Land and Building Rights Acquisition Duty (BPHTB). This study examines the influence of Trust in Authority, Power of Authority, Tax Morale, and Tax Awareness on local tax compliance, with Civic Pride as a moderating variable. Primary data were collected through an online Likert-scale questionnaire using Google Forms from 300 registered and active local taxpayers under the Regional Revenue Agency (Bapenda) of Lahat Regency. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that trust in tax authorities, perceived power of authority, tax morale, and tax awareness significantly affect local tax compliance, while Civic Pride strengthens these relationships. The study contributes to the Slippery Slope Framework and Theory of Planned Behavior by incorporating Civic Pride as a contextual moderator and provides practical insights for designing trust-based and participatory local tax policies

titulo: Who Absorbs Fiscal Adjustment? Transfer Composition and Local Budget Adaptation in Indonesia
palavras_chave: fiscal consolidation; intergovernmental transfers; local government spending; expenditure composition; capital expenditure; personnel costs; special allocation fund; Indonesia; regional budget
resumo: This study examines how changes in the composition of intergovernmental transfers are associated with the distribution of fiscal adjustment across local government expenditure in Indonesia. It compares three contrasting fiscal episodes is the 2020 emergency adjustment, the 2025 policy induced transfer recomposition, and the 2026 budget year adjustment. The analysis combines harmonized aggregate regional budget and intergovernmental transfer data for 2019–2026 with accounting decomposition, structured pattern comparison, and policy document triangulation. The findings show that fiscal adjustment is distributed unevenly across expenditure categories. In 2020, capital expenditure declined by 28.02%, compared with 3.03% for personnel expenditure. In 2025, a 0.91% increase in the aggregate central transfer allocation concealed substantial compositional changes, including a 65.35% reduction in physical special allocation funds, while realized capital expenditure declined by 20.80% and personnel expenditure increased by 3.83%. The 2026 budget shows a similar planned pattern, with capital expenditure declining by 29.55% compared with 1.18% for personnel expenditure. The study develops the concept of composition-sensitive fiscal transmission, emphasizing that fiscal adjustment should be assessed through the scale of transfer change, the composition of affected transfer instruments, and the expenditure incidence of adjustment.

titulo: Disentangling Fiscal Dependencies: Evidence from Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
palavras_chave: fiscal dependence; subnational fiscal autonomy; fiscal federalism; intergovernmental transfers; gross state product; Uttar Pradesh; Bihar; speed of adjustment; long-run equilibrium
resumo: This study examines the structural aspects of fiscal dependency of two states namely Uttar Pradesh and Bihar by analyzing the relationship between gross State Domestic Product and tax revenues which includes own tax revenue and share from center in tax devolution. The issue of subnational fiscal autonomy is crucial in the context of fiscal federalism, especially for governments with higher population and socio-economically challenged economies that mainly rely on intergovernmental transfers. In order to empirically examine the relationship among variables, the study uses Autoregressive Distributed lag Model (ARDL), which is well suited for time series analysis of mixed order of integration. The findings exhibit that both state’s GSDP is largely impacted by the share in the central tax than the own tax revenues. The impact of own tax revenue is negative while the share in the central tax is positive on the GSDP for both in long and short-term for both the states. The coefficient of co-integration equation highlights the disparity in the speed of convergence towards the long-run equilibrium. Bihar trails with 31% (speed of adjustment), perhaps as a result of smaller revenue bases and administrative difficulties, but Uttar Pradesh respond to economic shocks rather rapidly with 42% (speed of adjustment), indicating a more effective fiscal mechanism.

titulo: FINANCIAL SUPPORT OF REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT: ESSENCE, SOURCES, FORMS AND INSTRUMENTS
palavras_chave: regional development funding; state regional policy; decentralization reform; local self-government; fiscal capacity; post-conflict reconstruction; EU cohesion policy; blended finance; public-private partnerships; concession mechanism; industrial parks; regional development agencies; participatory budgeting; Ukraine
resumo: The article is devoted to a comprehensive theoretical and applied examination of the financial support of regional development, understood as a systemic phenomenon that connects the economic potential of a territory with the strategic goals of state regional policy. The relevance of the topic is determined by several interrelated circumstances that currently shape the environment in which Ukrainian regions and territorial communities operate. The first is the continuing consequences of the decentralisation reform, which substantially expanded the powers and the resource base of local self-government but simultaneously created a pronounced differentiation in the fiscal capacity of communities. The second is the impact of full-scale armed aggression, which has transformed the structure of local budget revenues, redistributed expenditure priorities towards defence and social protection, restricted access to borrowed resources and increased the dependence of many territories on intergovernmental transfers and external assistance. The third is the perspective of post-war reconstruction and European integration, which requires a financing architecture compatible with the principles of the European Union cohesion policy, including multiannual programming, co-financing, additionality and result orientation. The article discusses the conceptual boundaries of the category of financial support and compares the resource-based and the process-based interpretations that prevail in the economic literature. It considers the criteria according to which the sources of financing of regional development may be classified, including ownership, the level at which resources are generated, the degree of stability of receipts and the repayable or non-repayable nature of the funds involved. Considerable attention is devoted to the forms in which financial resources reach regional economic systems, namely self-financing, budgetary financing, lending, investment, grant-based support, and mixed or blended arrangements that combine public and private capital. The instrumental dimension of the problem is also addressed, covering programme-based budgeting, the State Fund for Regional Development, targeted subventions, local borrowing and municipal bond issuance, public-private partnership and concession mechanisms, industrial parks, regional development agencies, participatory budgeting and instruments of guarantee and insurance support. The paper further outlines the methodological difficulties of assessing the effectiveness of financial support, the institutional constraints that limit the use of market-based instruments at the local level, and the questions of coordination between national, regional and donor financing flows. The material is intended to contribute to the discussion on building a balanced and predictable model of financing regional development in Ukraine.

titulo: PERSEPSI DAMPAK PROGRAM MBG TERHADAP KETAHANAN EKONOMI KELUARGA
palavras_chave: free nutritious meals program; household economic resilience; consumption smoothing; flypaper effect; food aid; food security; household savings; household debt; economic productivity; psychological well-being; Jambi
resumo: Abstrak Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) merupakan intervensi kebijakan pemerintah Indonesia yang dirancang untuk meningkatkan pemenuhan gizi anak dan berpotensi mendukung ketahanan ekonomi rumah tangga. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis persepsi rumah tangga terhadap perubahan ketahanan ekonomi setelah pelaksanaan MBG di Provinsi Jambi. Data primer dikumpulkan dari 54 rumah tangga penerima manfaat yang dipilih secara purposif melalui kuesioner dengan pertanyaan tertutup dan terbuka. Ketahanan ekonomi dianalisis melalui enam dimensi, yaitu stabilitas pangan, efisiensi anggaran, kemampuan menabung dan pengelolaan utang, resiliensi terhadap guncangan, alokasi waktu dan produktivitas ekonomi, serta kesejahteraan psikologis. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa MBG membantu sebagian rumah tangga mengurangi tekanan konsumsi dan pengeluaran, tetapi manfaat terhadap ketahanan ekonomi secara keseluruhan masih parsial. Perubahan pada tabungan, utang, dan produktivitas ekonomi relatif terbatas. Kualitas dan penerimaan makanan juga berkaitan dengan kemampuan MBG menggantikan pengeluaran rumah tangga, sehingga pola yang ditemukan konsisten dengan mekanisme consumption smoothing dan flypaper effect. Kata kunci: MBG, Ketahanan ekonomi rumah tangga, Consumption smoothing, Bantuan pangan, Resiliensi ekonomi

titulo: Fiscal Performance Analysis of Local Government through an APBD-Based Financial Ratio Approach: Empirical Evidence from East Kalimantan Province, Indonesia (2020–2024)
periodico: Al-Kharaj Journal of Islamic Economic and Business
palavras_chave: fiscal decentralization; fiscal independence; fiscal capacity; regional financial management; APBD; financial ratios; intergovernmental transfers; income diversification; capital expenditure; expenditure structure; East Kalimantan
resumo: Fiscal decentralization has expanded the authority of local governments in managing regional financial resources; however, greater fiscal authority does not necessarily guarantee stronger fiscal independence and sustainable fiscal performance. Evaluating local government fiscal performance is therefore essential to assess the effectiveness of regional financial management, particularly in resource-rich provinces with complex fiscal structures. This study aims to analyze the fiscal performance of the East Kalimantan Provincial Government during 2020–2024 using an APBD-based financial ratio approach. This study employed a quantitative descriptive design using secondary data from the audited Regional Government Financial Reports (LKPD) of East Kalimantan Province for fiscal years 2020–2024. Fiscal performance was evaluated through several indicators, including fiscal decentralization ratio, fiscal independence ratio, fiscal dependency ratio, PAD effectiveness ratio, revenue-expenditure efficiency ratio, expenditure composition ratio, and fiscal growth ratio. The results indicate that East Kalimantan experienced strengthening fiscal capacity during the observation period, reflected in increasing regional revenue and consistently effective PAD realization. However, fiscal independence remained influenced by intergovernmental transfers, indicating that regional fiscal autonomy has not been fully achieved. The expenditure structure also shows a gradual increase in capital expenditure after the COVID-19 period, although operating expenditure remains the dominant component of regional spending. These findings demonstrate that strong fiscal capacity should be accompanied by revenue diversification, improved expenditure quality, and sustainable fiscal governance. This study contributes empirical evidence on the fiscal performance dynamics of a resource-rich Indonesian province during pandemic disruption and post-pandemic recovery, providing implications for strengthening local fiscal autonomy under the decentralization framework.

titulo: Budget federalism as a mechanism for equalizing the provision of merit goods to the regions
autores: Yulia I. Busheneva; N. P. Yemelyanov
palavras_chave: budget federalism; merit goods; subsidies and grants; regional equalization; regional typology; regional disparities; social infrastructure
resumo: Aim. To substantiate budget federalism measures aimed at equalizing the provision of merit goods to the population of regions, and to demonstrate the need for a transition from assessing budget capacity to assessing the accessibility of socially significant goods. Objectives. To characterize the forms of federal intergovernmental transfers and their significance for financing merit goods; to analyze the dynamics and functional structure of federal intergovernmental transfers in 2023–2025; to propose a typology of regions by dominant problems in the provision of merit goods to the population and to calculate the average grant dependency index for the identified types. Methods. The research employs methods of systemic, comparative, and structural analysis, a typologization method, and a calculation method. The information base consists of provisions of the budget legislation of Russia, data from the Ministry of Finance of Russia, the Federal Treasury, and scholarly publications devoted to issues of budget federalism, intergovernmental transfers, regional equalization, and social infrastructure. Results. It is established that in 2023–2025, the role of subsidies increased while the share of grants decreased in the structure of federal intergovernmental transfers, reflecting the growing importance of targeted program-project financing of the regions of Russia. A typology of regions of Russia is proposed depending on the dominant problems in the provision of merit goods to the population. The average grant dependency index is calculated taking into account the types of regions. It is shown that the highest formal degree of grant dependency is characteristic of regions with high vulnerability of families with children and regions with low population incomes. Conclusions. Budget federalism in the sphere of merit goods should be assessed not only by the volume of transfers and the level of grant dependency of regions but also by the ability of the instruments employed to reduce territorial disparities in the accessibility of education, healthcare, social protection, culture, and sports. Grants smooth out differences in budget capacity, but specific infrastructure and social deficits require a combination of grants, subsidies, subventions, other transfers, special standards, and intraregional redistribution. The results obtained in the study can be used in the formation of intergovernmental transfers taking into account dominant regional needs.

titulo: THE ROLE OF INTERGOVERNMENTAL TRANSFERS IN MITIGATING REGIONAL INEQUALITY IN UZBEKISTAN: EMPIRICAL ASSESSMENT AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVEMENT
palavras_chave: intergovernmental transfers; regional disparities; fiscal equalization; Theil index; Gini coefficient; Uzbekistan
resumo: The paper analyses the current state of the intergovernmental transfer system in Uzbekistan, changes in the revenue base of local budgets and the regional distribution of equalization transfers on the basis of official statistical data. Regional inequality is measured using the Theil index, the Gini coefficient and the coefficient of variation, while the progressivity of transfer allocation is assessed with a regression model. Based on the results, proposals are developed for transitioning the transfer system to formula-based equalization.

titulo: Are Government Transfers Sticky? Tracing The Flypaper Effect Across Indonesian Provinces
autores: Moh Danil; Andi Chairil Furqan; Rahmi Syafitri; Abdul Razik Luneto
palavras_chave: flypaper effect; fiscal transfers; regional government spending; special allocation fund; general allocation fund; revenue sharing fund; local own-source revenue; fiscal decentralization; local government financial independence; Indonesian provinces
resumo: Purpose: By examining the impact of general allocation funds (DAU), special allocation funds (DAK), revenue-sharing funds (DBH), and Locally-generated revenue (PAD) on regional expenditure from 2021 to 2025, this study aims to re-examine the phenomenon of the flypaper effect on Indonesian local governments. Research Method: Panel data regression analysis is the tool of choice for this quantitative investigation. This study's population comprises Indonesian provinces, and the sample comprises 165 panel observation points, collected through purposive sampling over a 5-year observation period. The EViews 14 program is used to process the data. Results and Discussion: Both the general allocation fund (DAU) and the revenue-sharing fund (DBH) positively affect regional expenditure. However, the effects are not statistically significant, according to the study's findings. However, locally generated revenue (PAD) and the Special Allocation Fund (DAK) have a significant positive effect on regional expenditure. These results demonstrate that reliance on federal transfer money has less impact on regional expenditure than the capacity of local governments to generate locally generated revenue. There is substantial evidence that DAK affects regional spending, although this impact is much lower than PAD's. This proves that the flypaper impact on regional expenditure is nonexistent. Implications: According to these results, local governments must continue working toward greater financial independence by making the most of PAD sources such as regional taxes, levies, and asset management. Meanwhile, it is the central government's responsibility to ensure that regional development is still supported through funding transfers. Originality: The results of this research disprove the hypothesis that regional expenditure by Indonesian provinces is subject to the flypaper effect.

titulo: FINANCIAL FRAMEWORK OF THE ECONOMIC SELF-SUFFICIENCY OF UKRAINE'S TERRITORIAL COMMUNITIES: CURRENT STATE AND DEVELOPMENT TRENDS
periodico: State and regions Series Economics and Business
palavras_chave: territorial communities; economic self-reliance; local budgets; fiscal decentralization; local own-source revenue; intergovernmental transfers; local self-government; public investment management; regional development instruments; Ukraine; full-scale war
resumo: The article examines the formation of the financial foundations of the economic self-sufficiency of territorial communities in Ukraine under contemporary socio-economic challenges. The relevance of the study is determined by the need to ensure the resilience of local self-government during the full-scale war, the growing demand for territorial recovery, and changes in the state's budgetary policy. The purpose of the study is to assess the current state of the financial support of territorial communities, identify trends in the development of local budgets, and analyze the impact of medium-term budget planning on the level of their economic self-sufficiency. The study analyzes the dynamics of the share of local governments' own-source revenues in GDP, the role of local budgets within the structure of Ukraine's consolidated budget, and the provisions of the Budget Declarations for 2025–2027, 2026–2028, and 2027–2029. The findings indicate that the fiscal decentralization reform significantly strengthened the financial role of territorial communities during 2015–2021. However, following the outbreak of the full-scale war, the centralization of budgetary resources intensified. The research demonstrates that the projected increase in the financial resources of local budgets in the medium term is not accompanied by a proportional increase in the financial autonomy of territorial communities. The main factors behind this trend include the continued redistribution of the military personal income tax (PIT), the growing role of intergovernmental transfers, the centralization of financing for specific public sectors, and limited funding for regional development instruments. At the same time, a positive trend is the introduction of a new public investment management system focused on strategic planning and the efficient use of budgetary resources. The study substantiates that ensuring the economic self-sufficiency of territorial communities in the long term requires restoring a balance between state support and the financial autonomy of local self-government, expanding the own-source revenue base of local budgets, fostering entrepreneurship, increasing the investment attractiveness of territories, and improving the efficiency of local resource management.

titulo: Analysis of Budget Efficiency on Acceleration of Development in Papua from the Point of Financial Governance
autores: Kajagi Kalman; Yulianus Pabassing; Herniati Herniati; Sri Iin Hartini
periodico: Greenation International Journal of Law and Social Sciences
palavras_chave: budget efficiency; special autonomy fund; Papua; special autonomy; fiscal architecture; Human Development Index; regional disparities; institutional capacity; flypaper effect; administrative sanctions; general principles of good governance; development paradox
resumo: Papua is one of the provinces with the largest budget in Indonesia through the Special Autonomy Fund mechanism, but the development paradox remains very real with high poverty rates and infrastructure lag. This study aims to analyze budget efficiency towards accelerated development in Papua viewed from the perspective of regional financial governance, with a normative juridical approach to the dynamics of Special Autonomy regulations post-Law Number 2 of 2021 and PMK Number 33 of 2024. The research method uses a qualitative descriptive-juridical approach with document analysis, literature study, and review of laws and regulations. The results of the study indicate that the fiscal architecture and implementation of Papua's special autonomy regulations face a paradox where the increase in the Special Autonomy Fund ceiling to 2.25 percent of the national DAU has not been followed by a proportional increase in institutional capacity; every 1 percent increase in the Special Autonomy Fund only contributes 0.198 percent to the Human Development Index (HDI) with widening disparities between regions, which from an administrative law perspective indicates a systemic violation of the principle of efficiency as required by Article 3 of Law Number 17 of 2003 concerning State Finance. Second, the factors inhibiting financial governance are structural and multidimensional, including weak human resource capacity of civil servants, fragmentation of planning between levels of government, dominance of operational expenditure, high Construction Cost Index, and the flypaper effect phenomenon which together create normative weaknesses in the form of legal vacuum, weak administrative sanctions, and low implementation of General Principles of Good Governance (AUPB).

titulo: Pengaruh Pendapatan Asli Daerah, Dana Alokasi Umum, Dana Alokasi Khusus, Dana Bagi Hasil, dan Produk Domestik Regional Bruto terhadap Belanja Daerah Kabupaten Pasaman
autores: Diva Pujana; Citra Ramayani; Jolianis Jolianis
palavras_chave: regional own-source revenue; general allocation fund; special allocation fund; revenue sharing fund; regional gross domestic product; regional government spending; fiscal decentralization; intergovernmental transfers; fiscal autonomy; Pasaman Regency; local government finance; fiscal capacity
resumo: Penelitian ini menganalisis pengaruh Pendapatan Asli Daerah (PAD), Dana Alokasi Umum (DAU), Dana Alokasi Khusus (DAK), Dana Bagi Hasil (DBH), dan Produk Domestik Regional Bruto (PDRB) terhadap Belanja Daerah Kabupaten Pasaman selama 2004–2024. Penelitian menggunakan 21 observasi tahunan dari Badan Pusat Statistik dan publikasi pemerintah daerah. Analisis EViews meliputi transformasi logaritma natural, uji Augmented Dickey–Fuller, diagnostik residual, Ramsey RESET, regresi linear berganda, dan pengujian signifikansi 5%. Estimasi utama menunjukkan PAD, DAU, DAK, dan DBH berpengaruh positif dan signifikan, dengan koefisien 0,191187; 0,564592; 0,164907; dan 0,235184. Model empat prediktor signifikan secara simultan (F = 539,0066; p < 0,001) dengan R-squared 0,992634. Uji Likelihood Ratio tambahan menunjukkan PDRB belum signifikan pada taraf 5% (p = 0,0577). Temuan menegaskan bahwa kapasitas belanja Pasaman berkaitan kuat dengan penerimaan daerah dan transfer antarpemerintah, terutama DAU. Penguatan kemandirian fiskal perlu disertai pengelolaan transfer yang produktif, akuntabel, dan berorientasi hasil. Hasil ini memberikan bukti empiris spesifik bagi pengelolaan fiskal Kabupaten Pasaman. This study examines the effects of Local Own-Source Revenue (PAD), the General Allocation Fund (DAU), the Special Allocation Fund (DAK), the Revenue Sharing Fund (DBH), and Gross Regional Domestic Product (GRDP) on regional expenditure in Pasaman Regency during 2004–2024. The study uses 21 annual observations from Statistics Indonesia and local government publications. EViews analysis includes natural-log transformation, the Augmented Dickey–Fuller test, residual diagnostics, Ramsey RESET, multiple linear regression, and 5% significance testing. The main regression shows positive and significant coefficients for PAD, DAU, DAK, and DBH of 0.191187, 0.564592, 0.164907, and 0.235184, respectively. The four-predictor model is jointly significant (F = 539.0066; p < 0.001) with an R-squared of 0.992634. An additional Likelihood Ratio test indicates that GRDP is not significant at the 5% level (p = 0.0577). The findings show that Pasaman Regency’s expenditure capacity is strongly associated with own-source revenue and intergovernmental transfers, particularly the General Allocation Fund. Fiscal autonomy should therefore be strengthened alongside productive, accountable, and outcome-oriented transfer management.

titulo: Analisis Flypaper Effect pada Belanja Daerah Kabupaten dan Kota di Provinsi Nusa Tenggara Barat Tahun 2021-2023
autores: Dinda Dwi Kirana; Siti Atika Rahmi; Sulhan Hadi
palavras_chave: flypaper effect; regional government spending; local own-source revenue; central government transfers; fiscal dependence; regional autonomy; fiscal decentralization; West Nusa Tenggara; common effect model; Chow test; score test; intergovernmental transfers; fiscal federalism; local government finance
resumo: Otonomi daerah menuntut pemerintah kabupaten/kota untuk membiayai Belanja Daerah dari dua sumber utama, yaitu Pendapatan Asli Daerah (PAD) dan Transfer Pemerintah Pusat. Idealnya, daerah mengutamakan PAD sebagai cerminan kemandirian fiskal, namun kenyataannya rasio ketergantungan terhadap dana transfer di banyak kabupaten/kota di Provinsi Nusa Tenggara Barat (NTB) masih berada di atas 70–80 persen, yang mengindikasikan potensi terjadinya flypaper effect, yaitu kondisi ketika Belanja Daerah lebih responsif terhadap dana transfer dibandingkan PAD. Penelitian ini bertujuan memperoleh bukti empiris mengenai fenomena flypaper effect pada Belanja Daerah kabupaten/kota di Provinsi NTB periode 2021–2023. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data panel dari 10 kabupaten/kota (8 kabupaten dan 2 kota) selama tiga tahun, sehingga diperoleh 30 observasi. Data sekunder bersumber dari Direktorat Jenderal Perimbangan Keuangan (DJPK) Kementerian Keuangan RI. Analisis dilakukan melalui statistik deskriptif dan regresi data panel, dengan pemilihan model estimasi menggunakan Uji Chow dan Uji Lagrange Multiplier. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa Common Effect Model (CEM) merupakan model terbaik. Hasil regresi menunjukkan variabel PAD tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Belanja Daerah (koefisien 0,90; probabilitas 0,3781 > 0,05), sedangkan Transfer Pemerintah Pusat berpengaruh positif dan signifikan (koefisien 0,55; probabilitas 0,0290 < 0,05). Secara simultan, kedua variabel berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Belanja Daerah (probabilitas F-statistik 0,0179), dengan kemampuan model menjelaskan variasi Belanja Daerah sebesar 25,77 persen (R² = 0,2577). Meskipun secara koefisien PAD lebih besar daripada Transfer, hanya variabel Transfer yang signifikan secara statistik, sehingga penelitian ini menemukan indikasi terjadinya flypaper effect pada Belanja Daerah kabupaten/kota di Provinsi Nusa Tenggara Barat, yang menandakan tingkat kemandirian fiskal daerah masih perlu ditingkatkan.

titulo: Equalization Funds and the Financing of Social Protection Services in Cameroonian Municipalities: A Critical Analysis
palavras_chave: equalization funds; social protection financing; local government finance; intergovernmental transfers; local fiscal capacity; need-based allocation; urban-rural disparities; transparency; decentralization
resumo: Social protection constitutes a major lever for poverty reduction and the fight against social inequalities.In Cameroon, the decentralization process has increased the responsibility of decentralized local governments in the provision of basic social services.However, their financial capacity remains limited, despite the existence of intergovernmental transfers and equalization mechanisms such as the General Decentralization Grant (Dotation Générale de la Décentralisation -DGD).This article examines the redistribution of equalization funds in support of social protection services at the municipal level, with a focus on the East and Far North regions of Cameroon.Using a mixed-methods approach that combines documentary analysis, surveys, and statistical tools (Pearson correlation and chi-square tests), the study assesses whether allocation practices comply with principles of equity and need.The findings reveal a significant gap between legislative frameworks and actual allocation practices, as well as a bias in favor of urban municipalities.These results highlight the urgent need to strengthen transparency and adopt needsbased redistribution mechanisms in order to improve the financing of social protection services at the local level.

titulo: Effectiveness and Efficiency of Regional Financial Governance at the Regional Financial and Asset Management Agency of Paser Regency, Indonesia, 2021–2025
autores: Nur Asni; Rifdan; Andi Cudai Nur; Andi Kasmawati
palavras_chave: fiscal decentralization; fiscal autonomy; revenue effectiveness; budget efficiency; budget absorption; intergovernmental transfers; local government revenue; Paser Regency; regional financial and asset management agency; public budgeting
resumo: This study aims to analyze the effectiveness and efficiency of regional financial governance in Paser Regency, East Kalimantan Province, Indonesia, during the 2021–2025 period. The study employs a descriptive quantitative approach using secondary data from the Paser Regency Budget Realization Reports for fiscal years 2021–2025, which were audited by the Audit Board of the Republic of Indonesia (BPK-RI). Effectiveness is assessed using the Revenue Effectiveness Ratio, Fiscal Decentralization Degree (DDF), and Regional Financial Independence Ratio (RKDK), while efficiency is assessed using the Expenditure Efficiency Ratio, Budget Absorption Ratio, and Expenditure Variance. The data are analyzed longitudinally to identify changes and trends in regional financial performance over the study period. The results show that Paser Regency generally achieved a very effective level of revenue realization. However, this performance was not accompanied by stronger fiscal capacity, as reflected in the relatively low contribution of locally generated revenue and continued dependence on intergovernmental transfers. In terms of efficiency, overall expenditure management remained inefficient, although budget absorption showed an increasing trend and actual expenditure remained below the approved budget throughout the study period. These findings indicate a gap between successful revenue target achievement, fiscal autonomy, and expenditure efficiency. The study implies the need to strengthen regional financial governance through the optimization of locally generated revenue, expenditure control based on revenue capacity, improved budget planning, and stronger monitoring and evaluation. For the Regional Financial and Asset Management Agency (BKAD) of Paser Regency, the findings provide a basis for developing financial management practices that move beyond revenue target achievement and budget absorption toward stronger fiscal autonomy and more efficient use of public resources.

titulo: Moderasi Dana Perimbangan pada Pengaruh Pendapatan dan Belanja Terhadap Kemandirian Keuangan Daerah Jawa Timur
autores: Devy Arisandi; Arifa Ilmiyati; Syifa Rohmah
palavras_chave: regional financial independence; balance funds; local taxation; regional levies; regional revenue; regional expenditure; fiscal decentralization; fiscal illusion; East Java regencies and cities; central transfers
resumo: Regional Financial Independence is an important indicator in fiscal decentralization, reflecting the ability of regions to finance regional expenditures without relying too much on transfers from the central government. Therefore, local governments must continue to optimize the management of regional financial resources to create good Regional Financial Independence. This study aims to determine the effect of Regional Taxes, Regional Levies, and Regional Expenditures on Regional Financial Independence and to determine whether the Balance Fund can moderate this influence. This research is a type of quantitative research using secondary data from the Regency/City APBD report in East Java Province. The data collection technique in this study used documentation techniques. The sample of this study amounted to 38 regencies/cities in East Java Province with a sampling technique that is saturated sampling. The data analysis method used in this study is panel data regression analysis with eviews13 software. The results showed that local taxes and levies have a positive and significant effect on Regional Financial Independence. Regional Expenditure has no effect on Regional Financial Independence. The Balance Fund can moderate by weakening the effect of Local Taxes on Regional Financial Independence. The Balance Fund cannot moderate the effect of Regional Retribution and Regional Expenditure on Regional Financial Independence. The implication of this research provides a strategic evaluation for local governments to reduce fiscal illusion by optimizing local resource management rather than relying heavily on central transfers.

titulo: O papel da reforma tributária na eficiência da administração pública municipal
palavras_chave: tax reform; municipal public administration; local government finance; consumption tax; destination principle; revenue redistribution; tax enforcement; revenue neutrality; intergovernmental transfers; tax administration efficiency
resumo: The Brazilian tax reform changed the structure of consumption taxation by introducing the Tax on Goods and Services and the Social Contribution on Goods and Services, with implications for municipal revenue collection, financial autonomy, and tax enforcement. This study aimed to analyze how these changes could influence the efficiency of municipal public administration, considering revenue distribution and the adaptation of tax controls. A qualitative, descriptive, and exploratory narrative literature review was conducted and supplemented by documentary analysis. Scientific articles published between 2020 and 2026 were consulted in specialized databases and journals, together with current constitutional and statutory legislation. Review articles, dissertations, theses, and conference papers were excluded. The analysis indicated that noncumulative taxation and the destination principle may reduce distortions and promote revenue redistribution, although their effects vary according to each municipality’s economic structure and institutional capacity. Aggregate revenue neutrality does not ensure local stability, as municipalities dependent on the Service Tax, transfers derived from the Tax on the Circulation of Goods and Services, or intergovernmental funds remain exposed to temporary losses. Data integration, electronic tax documents, coordinated enforcement, and staff training were identified as conditions for administrative efficiency gains. It was concluded that the reform may improve municipal tax administration, provided that equalization mechanisms, accounting planning, and technological infrastructure reduce disparities and preserve the financing of public services during the transition between tax systems, while accounting for differences in municipal size, own-source revenue, and dependence on intergovernmental transfers.

titulo: Corporate governance diversity, dividend pressure, and financial efficiency risk in Indonesian regional development banks: The moderating role of owner fiscal dependence
palavras_chave: board gender diversity; regional development banks; related-party lending; fiscal dependence; intergovernmental transfers; board of commissioners; bank governance; credit risk
resumo: This study examines how board gender diversity and dividend pressure relate to financial efficiency risk in Indonesian Regional Development Banks (Bank Pembangunan Daerah; BPDs), and whether the effect of related party loans (RPT) varies with the owner’s fiscal dependence on intergovernmental transfers. Using a balanced panel of 26 BPDs over 2018–2024 (N=182 bank-year observations), we estimate bank fixed-effects models with year effects and cluster-robust standard errors. Financial efficiency risk (FER) is a composite index capturing credit risk, operating inefficiency, and capital fragility (standardized NPL, BOPO, and −CAR). The findings indicate that while gender diversity on the board of directors and dividend pressure are not statistically significant in the baseline model, gender diversity on the board of commissioners is positively correlated with FER. At low levels of fiscal dependency, related-party lending intensity is negatively correlated with FER. However, there is a positive and substantial interaction between related-party lending and fiscal dependence. When owning governments rely heavily on intergovernmental transfers, the beneficial association of related-party lending declines and may even reverse, as seen by the conditional effect crossing zero at a fiscal-dependence value of roughly 0.896. By demonstrating that ownership-linked lending and board composition cannot be understood independently from subnational fiscal incentives in government-owned banks, the findings advance the field of bank governance research.

titulo: Macroeconomic Modelling of Xenophobia in South Africa: Foreign Owned SMES, Job Creation, and Economic -Wide Shocks if Migrant Entrepreneurs Exit
periodico: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
palavras_chave: xenophobia; immigrant entrepreneurs; job creation; GDP effects; unskilled labor; government revenue; budget deficit; unemployment; welfare distribution; fiscal sustainability; social exclusion; South Africa; social accounting matrix; computable general equilibrium simulation; accelerator theory; factor complementarity; government budget constraint; fiscal illusion
resumo: This study models the economy-wide effects of xenophobia-induced exit of foreign-owned small and medium enterprises in South Africa using a 2025 Social Accounting Matrix and a static Computable General Equilibrium model. Grounded in Mixed Embeddedness Theory (Kloosterman et al., 1999) and Social Accounting Matrix Theory (Pyatt & Round, 1985), the research disaggregates retail and transport activities into local and foreign ownership using FinMark Trust (2022), Statistics South Africa QLFS Q4 2023, and National Treasury (2025) data. Six hypotheses test GDP, employment, fiscal, and welfare impacts of 25%, 50%, and 75% exit shocks to foreign entrepreneurial capital and unskilled labour. Simulation results show a 50% exit reduces real GDP by 4.97%, exceeding the 4.0% threshold, consistent with General Equilibrium Theory (Scarf, 1967) and Accelerator Theory (Clark, 1917). South African unskilled employment falls by 5.92%, yielding a complementarity elasticity of 0.83, which supports Factor Complementarity Theory (Griliches, 1969) and rejects Substitution Theory (Borjas, 2003). Government revenue declines 7.80%, twice the GDP fall, validating Tax Buoyancy Theory (Sobel & Holcombe, 1996), while the budget deficit rises to 6.24% of GDP, breaching Fiscal Sustainability Theory (Blanchard et al., 1990). Unemployment increases by 3.19 percentage points, aligned with Search and Matching Theory (Mortensen & Pissarides, 1994). Equivalent Variation indicates regressive welfare losses: poor households lose 8.0% of income versus 3.0% for rich households, consistent with Social Exclusion Theory (Sen, 2000). The claim that expelling foreigners enables a R1 million annualstipend is refuted under Government Budget Constraint Theory (Domar, 1944): post-shock revenue is R1.66 trillion, making required funds 36.7 times available resources, confirming Fiscal Illusion Theory (Puviani, 1903). Limitations include the static model structure and reliance on survey-based disaggregation shares, per CGE Model Validation Theory (Kehoe, 2005). The study concludes that xenophobia functions as an adverse covariate shock under Social Risk Management Theory (Holzmann & Jorgensen, 2001), destroying institutional capital and reducing resilience as defined by Resilience Theory (Martin, 2012). Policy recommendations integrate Policy Coherence Theory (Hoebink, 2004): Home Affairs should permit foreign SMEs conditional on South African job ratios; National Treasury should counter Fiscal Illusion with citizen budgets; and DTIC should include compliant foreign firms in industrial policy per Industrial Policy Theory (Rodrik, 2004). The findings contribute to Mixed Embeddedness Theory by demonstrating macroeconomic embeddedness of migrant entrepreneurs through Linkage Theory (Hirschman, 1958).

titulo: The Determinants of Regional Government Expenditure in Districts/Cities in Sumatra
autores: Nora Susanti; Maria Maria; Riza Wahyudi
palavras_chave: regional government spending; local own-source revenue; general allocation fund; special allocation fund; flypaper effect; intergovernmental transfers; fiscal capacity; regencies and cities; Sumatra
resumo: Regional governments require fiscal capacity to support public services and development, with local own-source revenue, general allocation fund, and special allocation fund influencing regional expenditure. This study aims to examine the effect of local own-source revenue, general allocation fund, and special allocation fund on regional expenditure and identify the occurrence of the Flypaper Effect in regencies and cities in Sumatera during the 2022–2024 period. This study employed a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained through documentation methods from 154 local governments. The data were analyzed using panel data regression, coefficient of determination, t-test, and F-test. The results showed that simultaneously, local own-source revenue, general allocation fund, and special allocation fund significantly affected regional expenditure in Sumatera, with an F-statistic value of 97.13212. Partially, local own-source revenue had no significant effect on regional expenditure with a t-statistic value of 0.235865. Meanwhile, the general allocation fund and special allocation fund significantly affected regional expenditure with t-statistic values of 6.711569 and 5.572493, respectively. The findings also confirmed the occurrence of the Flypaper Effect, indicating that regional expenditure remains more responsive to intergovernmental transfers than local fiscal capacity. These results highlight the importance of strengthening local revenue sources to achieve greater regional fiscal independence.
